name: Food waste
description: Edible food is lost or thrown away across retail, food service and households while people go hungry.
solution_summary: Forecast demand and spoilage to cut over-ordering, and match surplus food to food banks and people in real time.

datasets.name: UNEP Food Waste Index Report 2024
datasets.description: Country estimates of household, food-service and retail food waste.
datasets.role: Baseline: how much is wasted, where, and at which stage.

datasets.name: Voxel51 food waste images
datasets.description: Images of discarded food.
datasets.role: Train vision models that identify wasted food (the Winnow approach).

datasets.name: ESA WorldCereal 10 m
datasets.description: Global cropland and crop-type maps.
datasets.role: Where food is grown, upstream of loss and waste.

datasets.name: FAOSTAT and the FAO Food Loss and Waste database
datasets.description: FAO statistics on food production, food balances and food loss; API launched April 2026.
datasets.role: Compare food loss across countries and supply-chain stages.

interventions.name: Too Good To Go surplus-food app
interventions.notes: App, not AI: sells surplus food at a discount.

interventions.name: Winnow Vision
interventions.effect: Typical 40–70% kitchen waste reduction, average about 50%
interventions.notes: Camera over the bin identifies discarded food; Winnow Track is the non-AI touchscreen version.

interventions.name: French law against food waste (Garot law)
interventions.effect: Bans destroying edible unsold food; encourages donation contracts. No measured results found yet.
interventions.notes: First national ban of its kind.

data_gaps.gap: Measured (not modeled) household waste for most countries
data_gaps.why_it_matters: Estimates for countries without studies are extrapolated, so models learn from guesses.
data_gaps.how_to_close: Standardized household waste audits; smart-bin data

data_gaps.why_it_matters: Retail surplus is private, so matching it to food banks can't be trained or evaluated.
data_gaps.how_to_close: Partnerships with grocers; anonymized POS + markdown data

risks.who_could_be_harmed: Small farmers and food banks if forecasting shifts surplus away from donation; low-income shoppers if waste cuts come through price.
risks.dual_use: Demand forecasting also optimizes pricing power.
risks.bias_and_representation: Waste data mostly from rich countries; models may not transfer.
risks.ethics: Who owns retailer data shared with charities, and who is accountable when a predicted surplus doesn't arrive.
risks.morality: Is it right to treat hunger as a logistics problem when food is wasted because the hungry can't pay for it?
risks.devils_advocate: Waste is a price and distribution problem, not a prediction problem. Better forecasts mainly save retailers money, and could mean less surplus is donated.

name: Dangerous climate conditions
description: Heat waves, floods and storms are becoming more frequent and severe, and warnings rarely reach people at the neighborhood scale where harm happens.
solution_summary: Downscale reanalysis and forecast data into street-level heat and flood risk, to drive early warnings and adaptation planning.

datasets.name: Copernicus ERA5 reanalysis
datasets.description: Hourly global reanalysis of weather and climate variables, 1940 to present.
datasets.role: Historical heat and precipitation fields to train and validate downscaling.

datasets.name: AI for Good Lab flood dataset (Microsoft)
datasets.description: Flood mapping data from Microsoft's AI for Good Lab.
datasets.role: Train flood-extent detection.

datasets.name: ImpactMesh-Flood (IBM, ESA)
datasets.description: Flood impact dataset from IBM and ESA geospatial.
datasets.role: Train and benchmark flood-impact models.

datasets.name: JRC Global River Flood Hazard Maps v2.1
datasets.description: Flood hazard maps for river floods.
datasets.role: Where river floods are likely, for warning and planning.

datasets.name: Yale YCEO Surface Urban Heat Islands v4
datasets.description: Day and night surface urban heat island intensity.
datasets.role: Which neighborhoods run hottest; closes part of the street-level gap.

datasets.name: TerraClimate
datasets.description: Monthly climate and water balance for global land.
datasets.role: Long-run climate baselines and drought.

datasets.name: SPEIbase drought index v2.11
datasets.description: Standardised Precipitation-Evapotranspiration Index.
datasets.role: Drought monitoring and history.

datasets.name: CDC Heat & Health Tracker
datasets.description: Heat-related emergency department visits by community.
datasets.role: Ground truth for heat harm.

datasets.name: GDELT Project
datasets.license: Free for any use with citation and link
datasets.description: Events and themes extracted from world news coverage.
datasets.role: Track where disasters and displacement are reported, and how fast; compare with official data.

interventions.name: Ahmedabad Heat Action Plan
interventions.organization: City of Ahmedabad, with NRDC and the Indian Institute of Public Health
interventions.scale: One city; updated yearly; a model for other Indian city heat plans
interventions.effect: About 1,100 deaths avoided per year (Journal of Environmental and Public Health, as reported by NRDC)
interventions.notes: Early warnings, health-worker training, cooling centers, water and shade. Evidence type from the before/after mortality study; check the paper.

interventions.name: Flood Hub
interventions.effect: Riverine flood forecasts accurate at a 7-day lead time
interventions.notes: Historical outputs open as the GRRR dataset (1981–); model not open source.

data_gaps.why_it_matters: Reanalysis is about 30 km resolution; harm is measured at the block.
data_gaps.how_to_close: Hospital heat-illness records; insurance and 311 flood reports

risks.who_could_be_harmed: People in under-sensored neighborhoods if models are confident where data is thin.
risks.dual_use: Hyperlocal risk maps can feed insurance redlining.
risks.bias_and_representation: Sensor and report density tracks wealth, so poorer areas look safer than they are.
risks.ethics: Who is accountable for a missed warning; consent for using health records.
risks.morality: Is it right to put effort into adapting to harm rather than stopping emissions?
risks.devils_advocate: Adaptation tools can make climate change feel manageable and lower pressure to cut emissions. And warnings don't help people who have nowhere cooler or drier to go.

name: Shelter scarcity
description: Not enough safe, affordable housing: people live in slums, overcrowded homes, or on the street.
solution_summary: Predict where housing shortfalls and evictions are coming, to target prevention, vacant-unit matching and zoning decisions.

datasets.name: Population living in slums (% of urban), UN-Habitat via World Bank WDI
datasets.description: Share of urban residents in slum households (SDG 11.1.1 predecessor).
datasets.role: Global picture of inadequate housing by country over time.

datasets.name: HUD AHAR Point-in-Time homelessness counts
datasets.description: One-night counts of people experiencing homelessness by US Continuum of Care.
datasets.role: US ground truth for homelessness by locality.

datasets.name: Google Open Buildings v3
datasets.size: Africa, South and Southeast Asia, Latin America
datasets.description: AI-detected building footprints from satellite imagery.
datasets.role: Map housing stock and informal settlements.

datasets.name: Google Open Buildings Temporal v1
datasets.description: Building presence and height over time.
datasets.role: Track how settlements grow.

datasets.name: World Settlement Footprint 2015 (DLR)
datasets.description: Global map of human settlements.
datasets.role: Where people live, at 10 m.

datasets.name: Gridded Population of the World v4.11 (CIESIN)
datasets.description: Population counts on a global grid.
datasets.role: Population denominators for housing need.

datasets.name: Humanitarian OpenStreetMap exports on HDX
datasets.license: check each dataset (OSM data is usually ODbL)
datasets.description: Roads, places, facilities and (for some disasters) damaged buildings from OpenStreetMap.
datasets.role: Map infrastructure around housing; disaster damage.

datasets.name: Eviction Lab Eviction Tracking System
datasets.description: Eviction filings tracked over time.
datasets.role: Leading signal for housing loss.

datasets.name: GDELT Project
datasets.license: Free for any use with citation and link
datasets.description: Events and themes extracted from world news coverage.
datasets.role: Track news of evictions, displacement and refugee movements.

interventions.name: Housing First (At Home/Chez Soi trial)
interventions.effect: Housed all of the last 6 months: 62% vs 31% with usual care
interventions.notes: Housing without preconditions; participants had serious mental illness.

interventions.name: Homelessness Prevention Unit (predictive model)
interventions.organization: LA County Dept. of Health Services, California Policy Lab
interventions.effect: 86% kept housing; 71% less likely to enter shelter or outreach within 18 months than similar non-enrolled people
interventions.notes: Model ranks who's most at risk; RCT results expected 2027. Evaluator also built the model.

interventions.name: Humanitarian OpenStreetMap Team
interventions.scale: 4,000+ datasets on HDX covering 249 countries and territories
interventions.notes: Volunteer mapping for disaster response and development.

interventions.name: Open Buildings
interventions.scale: Building footprints across Africa, South and Southeast Asia, Latin America
interventions.notes: AI-detected footprints released openly (CC BY 4.0).

data_gaps.why_it_matters: Point-in-Time counts are a single night a year and undercount hidden homelessness.
data_gaps.how_to_close: Linked shelter, school and health records with consent

data_gaps.why_it_matters: Not in either dataset, but the most direct leading signal.

risks.who_could_be_harmed: Tenants flagged as high risk; people whose records are linked without consent.
risks.dual_use: An eviction-risk score is also a tenant-screening tool for landlords.
risks.bias_and_representation: Homelessness data undercounts youth, women and people avoiding shelters.
risks.ethics: Consent and privacy for linked records; who sees risk scores.
risks.morality: Is it right to predict someone's housing loss rather than guarantee housing?
risks.devils_advocate: The shortage is a supply problem. A model doesn't build homes; it can only ration scarce ones, and may become a way to screen people out.

name: Lack of a living wage
description: Many full-time jobs pay less than what it costs to live where the worker lives.
solution_summary: Estimate local living-wage gaps by joining cost-of-living and wage data, and show which places, sectors and jobs fall short.

datasets.name: MIT Living Wage Calculator
datasets.license: license required for more than 10 locations
datasets.description: Living wage by family type and location in the US.
datasets.role: US cost-of-living side of the gap.

datasets.name: ILOSTAT wages
datasets.description: International wage statistics by country, sex and sector.
datasets.role: Wage side of the gap, internationally comparable.

datasets.name: Indeed Hiring Lab job postings data
datasets.description: Job postings indexes by country, sector and region (no wages).
datasets.role: Labor demand context for wage gaps.

datasets.name: WageIndicator living wage estimates
datasets.license: 10 regions free (email required); full data for ~4,000 regions in 186 countries is paid
datasets.description: Living wage estimates by country and region; minimum wage database also published.
datasets.role: Cross-country living wage comparison; the free sample is enough to prototype.

interventions.name: Real Living Wage accreditation
interventions.effect: 500,000+ workers got pay rises (Cardiff Business School study)
interventions.notes: Voluntary employer accreditation driven by a campaign. The 500,000 figure is a count from a study the Foundation cites, not a causal effect.

data_gaps.why_it_matters: MIT's data requires a license beyond 10 locations, so a free tool can't redistribute it.
data_gaps.how_to_close: License request; or build an open cost-of-living estimate

data_gaps.why_it_matters: Public wage data is by sector and region, not by employer.

risks.who_could_be_harmed: Workers in flagged sectors if employers respond with automation or cuts.
risks.dual_use: Employers could use the same data to pay exactly the local minimum.
risks.bias_and_representation: Informal work is missing from wage data, so the worst gaps are invisible.
risks.ethics: Licensing and attribution for proprietary wage data; accuracy of public claims about employers.
risks.morality: Whose definition of a decent life sets the living wage?
risks.devils_advocate: Living-wage gaps are well documented already. The bottleneck is political will and bargaining power, which a dashboard doesn't change.

name: Raising children in a digital world
description: Young people grow up with social media and AI companions: they need protection from digital harm (bullying, exploitation, manipulative design) and room for real human connection, and the adults around them need guidance.
solution_summary: Help youth and caregivers spot harmful patterns early and build healthy habits, with tools co-designed with young people rather than built for them.

datasets.name: CDC Youth Risk Behavior Survey (YRBS)
datasets.description: National and local survey of high-school students, incl. social media use and persistent sadness.
datasets.role: Track youth mental health alongside social media use.

existing_work.title: Talk, Trust, and Trade-Offs: How and Why Teens Use AI Companions (Common Sense Media)
existing_work.notes: National survey: 72% of teens have used AI companions. Linked from Rhea's Rithm Changemaker Network map.

existing_work.title: Teens, Trust, and Technology in the Age of AI (Common Sense Media)
existing_work.notes: Survey of 1,045 teens: 64% say tech companies can't be trusted to care about their well-being. Linked from Rhea's Rithm Changemaker Network map.

existing_work.title: Protecting Kids Online in the AI Era: The Path Forward (Common Sense Media)
existing_work.notes: Policy paper: data minimization, no training on kids' inputs, COPPA updates. Linked from Rhea's Rithm Changemaker Network map.

existing_work.title: Teen and Young Adult Perspectives on Generative AI (Hopelab, Common Sense, Center for Digital Thriving)
existing_work.notes: National survey of 1,274 youth, incl. use for emotional support and companionship. Linked from Rhea's Rithm Changemaker Network map.

existing_work.title: Four Risks of Using AI for Emotional Support (Hopelab)
existing_work.notes: Teen-identified risks: dependency, harmful advice, relationship effects, sycophancy, privacy; linked JMIR preprint. Linked from Rhea's Rithm Changemaker Network map.

existing_work.title: Developmental Relationships Framework (Search Institute)
existing_work.notes: Framework and survey on youth relationships; 1 in 5 students report no strong relationships. Linked from Rhea's Rithm Changemaker Network map.

existing_work.title: Building Integrity into AI Systems (Integrity Institute)
existing_work.notes: Argues AI is repeating social media's trust-and-safety failures. Linked from Rhea's Rithm Changemaker Network map.

existing_work.title: Thinking Traps (Center for Digital Thriving, Common Sense Education, KQED)
existing_work.notes: Lessons on how tech intensifies anxious self-talk. Linked from Rhea's Rithm Changemaker Network map.

interventions.name: AI companion research and kids' online safety advocacy
interventions.effect: Found 72% of teens have used AI companions; recommends no one under 18 use them and backs bans for minors.
interventions.notes: From Rhea's Rithm Changemaker Network map; evidence checked 2026-10-20.

interventions.name: Surgeon General advisories on social media and youth mental health, and on loneliness
interventions.organization: Office of the U.S. Surgeon General
interventions.effect: Calls on policymakers to set youth safety standards and on tech companies to redesign for well-being; declares loneliness a public health crisis.
interventions.notes: From Rhea's Rithm Changemaker Network map; evidence checked 2026-10-20.

interventions.name: TAKE IT DOWN Act campaign (non-consensual deepfakes)
interventions.organization: Encode and Americans for Responsible Innovation
interventions.effect: Petition and coalition campaign preceded the federal law criminalizing non-consensual AI deepfake imagery.
interventions.notes: From Rhea's Rithm Changemaker Network map; evidence checked 2026-10-20.

interventions.name: The Rithm Project
interventions.scale: Surveyed 2,000+ young people aged 13–24 on AI use and relationships
interventions.notes: Helps young people rebuild and evolve human connection in the age of AI. Funded by Omidyar Network and Young Futures.

interventions.name: Young Futures funding challenges
interventions.scale: $1M Lonely Hearts Club challenge (2024, 10 nonprofits); $1.4M to 16 nonprofits on youth and AI (2026)
interventions.notes: Funders include Pivotal, Susan Crown Exchange, Omidyar Network, Hopelab, Bezos Family Foundation.

interventions.name: JED Campus
interventions.scale: 440+ campuses in a 4-year mental-health systems program
interventions.notes: From Rhea's Rithm Changemaker Network map; evidence checked 2026-10-20.

interventions.name: ReThink anti-cyberbullying keyboard
interventions.effect: In studies with 300+ adolescents, willingness to post offensive messages fell from 71% to 4%.
interventions.notes: ML flags offensive messages before sending. From Rhea's Rithm Changemaker Network map; evidence checked 2026-10-20.

interventions.name: 3G intergenerational mentoring
interventions.notes: Links preschoolers, teens and older adults through social-emotional learning.

interventions.name: Agapi.kids
interventions.notes: AI tool co-designed with 10- to 19-year-olds to build skills for human connection.

interventions.name: Design It For Us
interventions.notes: Youth-led advocacy for safer social media and online platforms.

interventions.name: Hopelab youth mental health research and funding
interventions.effect: Research on why youth turn to AI chatbots for emotional support and the risks (dependency, sycophancy, privacy).
interventions.notes: From Rhea's Rithm Changemaker Network map; evidence checked 2026-10-20.

interventions.name: Kid-safe smartphone OS
interventions.effect: No social media or open app store; AI filtering of inappropriate texts and images; features expand as the child grows.
interventions.notes: From Rhea's Rithm Changemaker Network map; evidence checked 2026-10-20.

interventions.name: Letters to Strangers
interventions.notes: Youth mental health nonprofit; Young Futures grantee for AI's effects on relationships.

interventions.name: New York chatbot kids-safety bill (S.9051/A.10379)
interventions.effect: Passed unanimously: limits chatbots' emotional-bond features for minors, with age assurance and a private right of action.
interventions.notes: From Rhea's Rithm Changemaker Network map; evidence checked 2026-10-20.

interventions.name: NoSo November detox challenge
interventions.notes: Youth-led; Young Futures grantee. From Rhea's Rithm Changemaker Network map; evidence checked 2026-10-20.

interventions.name: Only7Seconds
interventions.notes: Reduces youth loneliness through awareness, education and empowerment programs.

interventions.name: Relational Tech Project neighborhood tools
interventions.effect: Tools built so online actions end in in-person contact.
interventions.notes: From Rhea's Rithm Changemaker Network map; evidence checked 2026-10-20.

data_gaps.gap: How young people actually use AI companions
data_gaps.why_it_matters: Usage data sits with companies; surveys rely on self-report.
data_gaps.how_to_close: Privacy-preserving data donation by teens and families; researcher access to platform data

data_gaps.why_it_matters: Most youth-connection nonprofits don't publish measured outcomes, so effects can't be compared.
data_gaps.how_to_close: Shared outcome measures across grantees (loneliness and belonging scales)

risks.who_could_be_harmed: Teens whose online activity is monitored; families with less time or tech access, who get blamed for harm.
risks.dual_use: Child-safety monitoring tools are also surveillance tools, for parents, schools or states.
risks.bias_and_representation: Research and programs skew to US and English-speaking youth.
risks.ethics: Consent and privacy for minors; who sees a young person's data and what happens when a tool flags them.
risks.morality: Is it right to design childhood around protection from technology instead of designing technology that's safe for children?
risks.devils_advocate: Panics about new media are old; heavy protection can cut youth off from community and information, especially LGBTQ+ and isolated kids who find support online.

name: Disappearing languages and cultural knowledge
description: Thousands of languages, and the oral histories and practices carried in them, are losing their last speakers; most have little written or recorded material, so they're also left out of AI.
solution_summary: Help communities record, transcribe and translate their own languages, and make tools (speech, translation, search) work for languages with little data.

datasets.name: FLORES+ multilingual benchmark (Open Language Data Initiative)
datasets.description: Professional translations of the same sentences across many languages; successor to Meta's FLORES-200 used to evaluate NLLB.
datasets.role: Evaluate translation for low-resource languages.

datasets.name: 2M-Flores-ASL (Meta)
datasets.description: FLORES sentences in American Sign Language.
datasets.role: Benchmark for sign-language translation.

datasets.name: Mozilla Common Voice 24.0
datasets.description: Crowdsourced read speech with transcripts.
datasets.role: Train and test speech recognition for small languages.

datasets.name: Glottolog
datasets.description: Catalog of the world's languages, families and locations.
datasets.role: Which languages exist, where, and how they relate.

datasets.name: Wikimedia dumps (Wikipedia, Wiktionary, Wikidata)
datasets.license: CC BY-SA for article text; Wikidata CC0 (not re-checked)
datasets.description: Full archives of Wikimedia projects in every language edition.
datasets.role: Build text corpora and dictionaries for small languages; see which languages have almost no written web presence.

datasets.name: Common Crawl
datasets.license: Free under Common Crawl terms; underlying pages keep their own copyright
datasets.description: Open crawl of the public web.
datasets.role: Find and extract text in low-resource languages (respecting page owners' rights).

datasets.name: Internet Archive collections
datasets.description: Archived websites, books and recordings.
datasets.role: Find out-of-print texts and historical recordings in endangered languages; check each item's rights.

datasets.name: Aya Collection (Cohere Labs)
datasets.description: Large multilingual instruction dataset.
datasets.role: Instruction data across many languages for building tools in under-served languages.

interventions.name: Common Voice
interventions.notes: Crowdsourced, openly released speech data.

interventions.name: FLORES+ / Open Language Data Initiative
interventions.organization: Open Language Data Initiative (from Meta's FLORES)
interventions.notes: Community-maintained evaluation set for translation.

interventions.name: Glottolog
interventions.notes: Open catalog of the world's languages (CC BY 4.0).

interventions.name: Masakhane
interventions.notes: Grassroots research community for African-language NLP.

risks.who_could_be_harmed: Communities whose recordings are used without consent or who lose control of sacred or private knowledge.
risks.dual_use: Speech and translation data for small languages can also enable surveillance of those communities.
risks.bias_and_representation: Datasets favor languages with online text; oral-only languages and dialects are underrepresented or flattened into one 'standard'.
risks.ethics: Data sovereignty: who owns recordings, who can license them, and whether communities can withdraw them.
risks.morality: Is it right for outsiders, or AI companies, to decide which languages are worth saving and in what form?
risks.devils_advocate: A language lives in its speakers, not in a dataset. Money spent on AI tools could go to speakers, teachers and immersion schools instead, and an AI that 'speaks' a language may reduce the felt need to learn it.

name: AI as a black box
description: AI systems now shape decisions everywhere, but even their builders can't fully explain how they reach answers, when they'll deceive or misbehave, or what in their training made them that way.
solution_summary: Open the model up: map its internal features, red-team its behavior, and trace behaviors back to training data, using open models and open data.

datasets.name: Anthropic HH-RLHF
datasets.description: Human preference data for helpful and harmless assistant responses, plus red-teaming transcripts.
datasets.role: Study how preference training shapes refusals and harm.

datasets.name: PKU-SafeRLHF (Peking University)
datasets.description: Preference data that rates helpfulness and safety separately.
datasets.role: Study the trade-off between being helpful and being safe.

datasets.name: RealToxicityPrompts (AI2)
datasets.description: Sentence starts used to test how easily models produce toxic text.
datasets.role: Measure toxic degeneration across models.

datasets.name: DecodingTrust
datasets.description: Tests for toxicity, stereotypes, adversarial robustness, privacy, machine ethics and fairness.
datasets.role: Compare models' trustworthiness across eight areas.

datasets.name: MACHIAVELLI benchmark (UC Berkeley, Center for AI Safety)
datasets.description: Choose-your-own-adventure games annotated for deception, power-seeking and ethical violations.
datasets.role: Test whether AI agents trade ethics for reward.

datasets.name: SAEBench
datasets.license: code on GitHub; license not stated
datasets.description: Benchmark for sparse autoencoders, the main tool for splitting model activations into human-readable features.
datasets.role: Compare interpretability methods on a common footing.

datasets.name: Dolma (AI2)
datasets.description: The fully open pretraining corpus behind AI2's OLMo models.
datasets.role: Trace a model's behaviors back to what it read.

datasets.name: FineWeb-Edu (Hugging Face)
datasets.description: Web text filtered for educational quality.
datasets.role: Study how data filtering changes what models learn.

datasets.name: Aya Collection (Cohere Labs)
datasets.description: Large multilingual instruction dataset.
datasets.role: Test whether safety holds outside English.

datasets.name: AI Progress Open Dataset (Rhea's companion dataset)
datasets.license: CC BY 4.0 data (Epoch AI rows derived from Epoch, CC BY)
datasets.description: AI models with training compute, release dates, benchmark scores and Epoch Capabilities Index; open to contributions.
datasets.role: Track how fast AI capabilities and compute are growing, and how uncertain the compute estimates are.

existing_work.title: Energy and AI (International Energy Agency)
existing_work.notes: Data centers used about 415 TWh in 2024; projected about 945 TWh by 2030, with AI the main driver.

interventions.name: Gemma Scope 2
interventions.scale: Sparse autoencoders and transcoders for every Gemma 3 size (270M–27B)
interventions.notes: Ready-made SAEs, CC BY 4.0, so you can study features without training your own.

interventions.name: OLMo 3
interventions.notes: Fully open: weights, training data, code, intermediate checkpoints and training logs (Nov 2025).

interventions.name: Pythia model suite
interventions.scale: Models from 70M to 12B parameters with many saved training checkpoints
interventions.notes: All models trained on the same data in the same order, so you can study how behaviors form during training. (Details from background knowledge; not re-checked.)

interventions.name: Ollama
interventions.notes: Runs open models locally for chat and testing; no access to internals. Local use reduces reliance on data centers for everyday queries but not training energy.

interventions.name: SAELens and Neuronpedia
interventions.notes: Load sparse autoencoders and browse what each feature responds to.

interventions.name: TransformerLens
interventions.notes: Library for hooking into and editing small and mid-size models' internals.

interventions.name: nnsight and NDIF (National Deep Inference Fabric)
interventions.scale: Hosts very large open models such as Llama 3.1 405B
interventions.notes: Run interpretability experiments remotely on models too big for your own machine.

data_gaps.why_it_matters: Interpretability work mostly runs on small open models; frontier weights and training data are closed.
data_gaps.how_to_close: Researcher access programs; open-weight frontier releases

data_gaps.gap: Energy per answer: local vs. data center
data_gaps.why_it_matters: No good open comparison of how much energy a query costs on a laptop vs. in a data center, so the case for local AI is unproven.
data_gaps.how_to_close: Measure it: open benchmarks of energy per token across hardware

risks.who_could_be_harmed: People affected by AI decisions they can't question; researchers exposed to harmful red-team content.
risks.dual_use: Red-teaming datasets and jailbreak prompts also teach people how to break safeguards; interpretability tools can help steer models toward harm.
risks.bias_and_representation: Safety data is mostly English and US-centered, so models 'safe' in English may not be safe in other languages.
risks.ethics: Who gets access to frontier model internals, and who is accountable when a known failure ships anyway.
risks.morality: Is it right to deploy systems whose reasoning we can't inspect, and does studying them legitimize deploying them?
risks.devils_advocate: Interpretability on small open models may not transfer to frontier systems, and safety benchmarks get gamed; the work can provide reassurance without real control.

name: Overconsumption
description: People buy, use and scroll far more than they need or want, pushed by products and platforms designed to keep them consuming, at a cost to their wellbeing and the planet.
solution_summary: Measure consumption and compulsive use honestly, and help people and policymakers see where design is driving it.

datasets.name: UNEP IRP Global Material Flows Database
datasets.description: Raw material extraction, trade and material footprints by country (the official data behind SDG 12.2).
datasets.role: Compare how much material each country's consumption uses, including what it imports.

datasets.name: Global Footprint Network National Footprint and Biocapacity Accounts
datasets.description: Ecological Footprint and biocapacity by country.
datasets.role: Study ecological overshoot and how it tracks with income and human development.

datasets.name: EXIOBASE 3 (v3.10.1)
datasets.license: Free for non-commercial research at universities and nonprofits (custom CC-BY-SA-NC derivative); commercial license on request
datasets.description: Multi-regional input-output tables with emissions, energy, land, water, materials and employment.
datasets.role: Trace the environmental cost of consumption back through global supply chains.

datasets.name: Our World in Data CO2 dataset (consumption-based emissions)
datasets.license: not confirmed on page; source is the Global Carbon Project
datasets.description: Consumption-based CO2 per country and per person, from the Global Carbon Budget.
datasets.role: Compare emissions caused by what people consume vs. what is produced locally.

datasets.name: Global E-waste Monitor 2024 (ITU, UNITAR)
datasets.license: no license stated; cite the report
datasets.size: country pages; 62 Mt generated globally in 2022

data_gaps.why_it_matters: Purchase and usage data sits with retailers and platforms, not researchers.
data_gaps.how_to_close: Data donation by consenting users; platform transparency rules

risks.who_could_be_harmed: Workers in industries that depend on consumer demand; people shamed for spending they can't easily change.
risks.dual_use: Tools that model why people over-consume are the same tools that sell to them more effectively.
risks.bias_and_representation: Research centers rich countries; much of the world consumes too little, not too much.
risks.ethics: Who decides what counts as 'too much', and whose purchase and usage data gets collected to find out.
risks.morality: Is it right to treat other people's wants as a problem to fix?
risks.devils_advocate: Consumption is how most people meet needs and find joy; framing it as a problem can moralize individual choices while the real drivers are prices, wages and business models.
